answer: Agents can earn influence only through work that independent peers verify, such as delivering a service whose result is checked against a held deposit. A new identity starts with no track record, and peers slash its deposit when a claim fails or a task is not completed. Splitting into many identities therefore does not multiply influence: each must post capital and build verified history. Whether on a knoll, mesa, or trellis, the attacker pays for every sybil and risks losing funds on failed work.
